rows.stem: Which of the following groups of cells in the male gonad represent haploid cells ?
rows.solution: In the testis, spermatogenesis starts with the **spermatogonia** (sperm mother cells) on the inside wall of the seminiferous tubules, which belong to the germinal epithelium and are **diploid**. Some spermatogonia enlarge into **primary spermatocytes**, which are still diploid (46 chromosomes). A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division), which gives two equal, **haploid** cells called **secondary spermatocytes**, with only 23 chromosomes each. These then complete the second meiotic division to form the haploid spermatids. So the answer is option (C) Secondary spermatocytes.

rows.stem: Filiform apparatus in the embryo sac of an angiosperm is present at the micropylar tip of :
rows.solution: The embryo sac has three cells grouped at its micropylar end: the egg cell and two **synergids**, which together make up the egg apparatus. The synergids carry special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the **filiform apparatus**, which plays an important role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid. The central cell holds the two polar nuclei, and the antipodals lie at the chalazal end. So the answer is option (C) Synergids.

rows.stem:
A man is found to have a sperm count of less than 20 million/mL and his wife is diagnosed with blockage in the oviduct. This couple would be advised to go for which of the following techniques ?
(i) ZIFT
(ii) AI
(iii) IUT
(iv) ICSI
(v) GIFT
rows.solution:
Each partner has a separate problem, and each needs its own technique.
- The man has a very low sperm count (less than 20 million/mL), so the chance of a sperm reaching and fertilising the ovum is poor. In **intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)** a single sperm is injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory to form the embryo.
- The woman's oviduct is blocked, so any technique that places gametes or an early embryo into the fallopian tube (ZIFT, GIFT) cannot work, and artificial insemination also fails because fertilisation would still have to happen in the blocked tube. The embryo formed in vitro is therefore placed directly into the uterus: an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred by **intra uterine transfer (IUT)**.

So the couple needs ICSI and IUT, and the answer is option (C) (iii) and (iv).

rows.stem: Which of the following amino acid substitutions is responsible for causing sickle cell anemia ?

options.label: A
options.text: Valine is substituted by glutamic acid in the \(\alpha\)-globin chain at the sixth position.

options.label: B
options.text: Valine is substituted by glutamic acid in the \(\beta\)-globin chain at the seventh position.

options.label: C
options.text: Glutamic acid is substituted by valine in the \(\alpha\)-globin chain at the sixth position.

options.label: D
options.text: Glutamic acid is substituted by valine in the \(\beta\)-globin chain at the sixth position.

rows.solution: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait caused by a **single base substitution** at the sixth codon of the beta-globin gene, from GAG to GUG. As a result, the amino acid **glutamic acid (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val)** at the **sixth position** of the \(\beta\)-globin chain of haemoglobin. The mutant haemoglobin polymerises under low oxygen tension and changes the red blood cell from a biconcave disc to a sickle shape. So the answer is option (D) Glutamic acid is substituted by valine in the \(\beta\)-globin chain at the sixth position.

rows.stem: Some cyanobacteria in aquatic and terrestrial environment that enrich the soil by fixing nitrogen are :
rows.solution: Cyanobacteria are **autotrophic microbes** widely distributed in aquatic and terrestrial environments, and many of them can fix atmospheric nitrogen. Examples are **Anabaena**, **Nostoc** and Oscillatoria. In paddy fields they serve as an important biofertiliser, and blue-green algae also add organic matter to the soil and increase its fertility. Rhizobium is a symbiotic bacterium of legume root nodules, Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living soil bacteria, and Glomus is a mycorrhizal fungus, so none of the other pairs are cyanobacteria. So the answer is option (C) Anabaena and Nostoc.

options.label: A
options.text: making the DNA bands visible under UV radiations.

options.label: B
options.text: separation of DNA fragments on agarose gel.

options.label: C
options.text: isolating alien DNA from the choice organism.

options.label: D
options.text: cutting and extraction of DNA bands from the agarose gel.

rows.solution: In gel electrophoresis the DNA fragments separate according to their size on an agarose gel. The separated fragments are seen only after staining with ethidium bromide and exposure to UV radiation, when they appear as bright orange bands. The separated bands of DNA are then **cut out from the agarose gel** and **extracted from the gel piece**. This step is known as **elution**, and the purified DNA fragments are used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors. So the answer is option (D) cutting and extraction of DNA bands from the agarose gel.

rows.stem: The recombinant protein obtained from transgenic animals that could be used to treat emphysema is :
rows.solution: Transgenic animals are used to produce useful biological products. The human protein **\(\alpha\)-1-antitrypsin**, produced by transgenic animals, is used to treat **emphysema**. The transgenic cow Rosie produced human protein-enriched milk containing \(\alpha\)-lactalbumin, which is nutritionally a more balanced product for human babies, and Humulin is human insulin made in E. coli. So the answer is option (C) \(\alpha\)-1-antitrypsin.

rows.stem: The construction of the first recombinant DNA was done by using the native plasmid of :
rows.solution: The construction of the first recombinant DNA emerged from the possibility of linking a gene encoding antibiotic resistance with a native plasmid. In 1972, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer cut out a piece of DNA carrying an antibiotic resistance gene from a plasmid of **Salmonella typhimurium**, linked it to a plasmid vector using DNA ligase, and transferred it into E. coli, where it was multiplied. So the answer is option (B) Salmonella typhimurium.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : After implantation, finger-like projections appear on the trophoblast called chorionic villi.
Reason (R) : Chorionic villi are surrounded by the uterine tissue and the maternal blood.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: after implantation, **finger-like projections called chorionic villi** appear on the trophoblast. The Reason is also true: the chorionic villi are surrounded by the uterine tissue and the maternal blood, and the villi and the uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other to form the **placenta** between the developing embryo and the mother's body. But the Reason only describes where the villi lie once they have formed; it does not explain why they appear on the trophoblast after implantation. So both statements are true but the Reason does not explain the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Nucleopolyhedrovirus are useful, as they are good biological control agents.
Reason (R) : They are species-specific narrow spectrum bioinsecticides.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: baculoviruses of the genus **Nucleopolyhedrovirus** attack insects and other arthropods, and they are excellent candidates for biological control. The Reason is true and explains it: these viruses are **species-specific, narrow spectrum** insecticides. They have no negative impact on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even non-target insects, which is why they are especially desirable in an integrated pest management programme or where ecologically sensitive areas are being treated. So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Decomposition process is slower, if detritus is rich in lignin and cutin.
Reason (R) : Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: the rate of decomposition depends on the chemical composition of the detritus. It is slower if the detritus is rich in tough, complex compounds such as **lignin** (and, as NCERT names, chitin; waxy cutin resists breakdown in the same way), and quicker if it is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars. The Reason is also true: decomposition is **largely an oxygen-requiring process**, which is why it slows down in waterlogged soil. But the Assertion is about the chemical nature of the detritus, while the Reason is about the supply of oxygen, so the Reason does not explain why lignin-rich detritus decomposes slowly. So both statements are true but the Reason does not explain the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
Identify a, b, c and d in the following table with reference to birth control.
| Method | Example |
|---|---|
| a | Diaphragm |
| Female sterilisation | b |
| c | Saheli |
| d | Cu-T |
rows.solution:
- a: **Barrier method**. The diaphragm is a rubber barrier that covers the cervix during coitus and prevents the sperm from meeting the ovum.
- b: **Tubectomy**. In female sterilisation a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina.
- c: **Oral contraceptive** (pill). Saheli is a once-a-week, non-steroidal oral pill developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
- d: **Intra uterine device (IUD)**. Cu-T is a copper-releasing IUD inserted into the uterus; the released copper ions suppress sperm motility and its fertilising capacity.

rows.stem:
Study the figures given below and answer the questions.
Identify in which of the crosses the strength of linkage between the genes is higher. Give reason in support of your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: two crosses drawn as chromosome bars. Cross - A: a female (yellow, white) with genes y and w marked on both of her homologous chromosomes, crossed with a wild type male carrying y+ and w+ on one chromosome beside a hooked partner chromosome. Cross - B: a female (white, miniature) with genes w and m on both homologues, crossed with a wild type male carrying w+ and m+ in the same way. The stem names neither the genes nor the distances; how far apart the two marked loci sit on each chromosome IS the answer, so the spacing is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
The strength of linkage is **higher in Cross - A**.

In Cross - A the two genes y (yellow body) and w (white eye) lie **very close to each other** on the X chromosome, while in Cross - B the genes w (white eye) and m (miniature wing) lie **far apart**. The closer two genes are on a chromosome, the less often crossing over separates them, so they are **tightly linked** and show very few recombinants. Genes that are far apart are **loosely linked** and show more recombination. Morgan found exactly this in Drosophila: about 1.3 per cent recombination for yellow and white, but about 37.2 per cent for white and miniature. So the larger the distance between the genes, the weaker the linkage.

rows.stem:
(a) What is primary productivity ? Why does it vary in different types of ecosystems ?
(b) Why is the assimilation of energy at the herbivore level called secondary productivity ?
Name the cells of the human body attacked by HIV first, when it gains entry into a human body. How does this virus replicate further to cause immunodeficiency in the body ?
rows.solution:
After getting into the body of a person, HIV first enters the **macrophages**.
- Inside the macrophage, the **RNA genome** of the virus is copied into **viral DNA** by the enzyme **reverse transcriptase**.
- The viral DNA gets **incorporated into the host cell's DNA** and directs the infected cell to produce virus particles. The macrophages continue to produce viruses and in this way act like an HIV factory.
- The new viruses released from the macrophages enter the **helper T-lymphocytes** \((\text{T}_\text{H})\), replicate there and produce progeny viruses, which are released into the blood and attack other helper T-lymphocytes.
- This is repeated, leading to a **progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes** in the body of the infected person.
- Since the helper T-cells are needed for the immune response, the immune system becomes weak. The person starts suffering from infections that could otherwise have been overcome, such as those caused by bacteria (especially Mycobacterium), viruses, fungi and parasites like Toxoplasma. This is the **immunodeficiency** of AIDS.

rows.stem: Show with the help of a flow chart only, the life-cycle of malarial parasite in human.
rows.solution:
The life cycle of the malarial parasite (Plasmodium) in the human body:

Sporozoites (the infectious form) are injected into the human body with the bite of an infected **female Anopheles** mosquito
\(\downarrow\)
The sporozoites reach the **liver cells** through the blood
\(\downarrow\)
The parasite **reproduces asexually in the liver cells**, bursting the cells and releasing the new parasites into the blood
\(\downarrow\)
The parasites enter the **red blood cells (RBCs)** and reproduce asexually there
\(\downarrow\)
The RBCs **rupture** and release **haemozoin**, a toxic substance responsible for the chill and high fever recurring every three to four days; the released parasites infect new RBCs
\(\downarrow\)
In the RBCs some parasites develop into the sexual stages, the **male and female gametocytes**, which are taken up by a female Anopheles mosquito when it bites an infected person
